title: claude_model_tiers.py: single source of truth for LEXI's Claude model-tier defaults, upgraded to the current top-tier models (currently the stale claude-sonnet-4-6/claude-opus-4-8 literal strings duplicated across main.py, cluster_endpoints.py, investigation_engine.py, and pinned into tests)
question: LEXI's backend selects a Claude model per query-difficulty tier via `os.environ.get("CLAUDE_MODEL", "claude-sonnet-4-6")` (simple/medium tiers) and `os.environ.get("CLAUDE_MODEL_COMPLEX", "claude-opus-4-8")` (complex tier) -- both stale Claude 4.x literals, duplicated across at least 4 call sites in main.py plus cluster_endpoints.py and investigation_engine.py, with tests/test_chat_live_fixes.py asserting directly against the literal string. A routine model bump means finding and changing every occurrence by hand, and a missed one silently keeps calling an old model. This is the exact scattered-literal pattern Pantheon's own src/config/models.mjs was built to fix for itself. The user has explicitly asked for the defaults themselves to be upgraded to the best currently available models, not merely centralized as-is -- does a single-source module fix both the duplication AND the staleness in a form LEXI's backend can adopt without a rewrite?
goal:
Create lexi-dashboard/backend/claude_model_tiers.py. It must export exactly one function: `model_id(tier)`.

Behavior, precisely:

1. A module-level dict (any name, not exported) holds the UPGRADED defaults -- current top-tier Claude 5 models, per explicit user instruction, replacing the stale Claude 4.x literals the codebase uses today:
   - `"CLAUDE_MODEL"`: `"claude-sonnet-5"`
   - `"CLAUDE_MODEL_COMPLEX"`: `"claude-opus-5-5"`
2. `model_id(tier)` looks up `tier` (the env-var name, e.g. `"CLAUDE_MODEL"`) in that dict to get the default, then returns `os.environ.get(tier, default)` -- an environment variable of that same name, when set, still overrides the default exactly as it does today at every existing call site.
3. If `tier` is not one of the known keys, raise `KeyError` (do not return `None` or a made-up string).

This is the WHOLE file: one dict, one function, `import os`, nothing else. No other exports.

Do NOT touch main.py, cluster_endpoints.py, investigation_engine.py, or any other file that currently calls `os.environ.get("CLAUDE_MODEL", ...)` directly -- wiring those call sites to use `model_id()` instead, which is also when the actual runtime behavior change takes effect, is deliberately a separate, later change, not this ticket. This ticket only creates the one new file.

The acceptance command is `python3 -m pytest tests/test_models_config.py -q`, which is already present (do not edit it) and self-contained -- it does not import main.py or anything that needs FastAPI/SQLModel/SQLCipher, so it runs standalone.
constraints: plain module-level code, no classes needed

do NOT name this file models.py -- lexi-dashboard/backend/models.py already exists as the real SQLModel database-schema module (Timeline, TimelineAnnotations, etc.) and a same-named file would silently shadow or collide with it
the two literal default strings must be exactly claude-sonnet-5 and claude-opus-5-5 -- the upgraded models, not the current stale ones
forbidden: do not elect a vendor as judge
do not edit any test file
do not edit main.py, cluster_endpoints.py, investigation_engine.py, requirements.txt, or any file other than claude_model_tiers.py
do not create or edit anything named models.py
